taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and Flora of North America.

evidence: Hays — UT PRC Purola Preserve records the species among naturally occurring, non-introduced plants.
Travis — UT PRC Travis County herbarium includes multiple Matelea reticulata specimens.
Williamson — UT PRC Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed county treatment.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county inferred from statewide or ecoregion range. Legacy names are counted only where taxonomic concept is reconciled.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at the flower first: broad flat pale-green lobes are strongly netted with dark green lines, and the center has conspicuous silvery reflective anther appendages—the 'pearl.'
diagnostic_traits: opposite deeply cordate leaves; stems and petioles conspicuously hairy
rotate broad corolla lobes strongly dark-reticulate and glabrous adaxially
corona reduced to a very low yellow undulate ring
8–15 cm fusiform follicle, sparsely to moderately muricate

confusers.separator: M. reticulata is flatter and strongly net-reticulated, glabrous inside, denser-haired, with a highly reduced corona and silvery center; M. edwardsensis is more campanulate with mostly longitudinal lines, hairy inside, and obvious fleshy corona segments.
Anglepod has larger uniformly olive-green non-reticulate flowers and a smooth sharply angled fruit; pearl milkvine has netted flowers and a muricate follicle.
